notes.title: Interest Rates and Stock Prices: An Old Debate Flares up!
notes.text: Rose strongly in the first eight months of 2026. On days the 10-year yield rose more than 3 bp the index fell about half a percent on average, and rose about half a percent when it fell. Analysts' 2026-27 earnings estimates rose more than 11%, the main reason equities held up. Technology aggregate return 25.22% but the median tech company only 7.75%, so gains were concentrated in the largest firms. No valuation call.

notes.title: The Price of Risk: An Equity Risk Premium Monologue!
notes.text: Implied ERP 4.23% at the start of 2026, 4.37% at the start of March and 4.51% by March 13 (index fell Feb 27-Mar 13 while oil rose above $100). Stocks look richly priced on P/E and dividend yield but the implied ERP is "in line" with the 65-year US average. Not clearly over- or undervalued; the market seems too sanguine about catastrophic risk. Historical-premium methods would have given roughly 5.5% to 14.5%.

notes.title: A "Fairly Highly Valued" Market: A Fed Chair Opines on Stocks, but should we listen?
notes.text: Fell 14.3% to the April 8 bottom then rose 13.7% year to date through Q3. notes.title: DeepSeek crashes the AI Party: Story Break, Change or Shift?

He valued it at $87 a share in September 2024 (price $109) and $78 in January 2025 (price $123), overvalued both times. The stock lost more than 10% in the week after DeepSeek. He sold half his stake in summer 2023 and another quarter in summer 2024 and still held a sizable position.

Raised AI target revenue from $80 billion to $160 billion but cut its target margin from 45% to 25%; space target margin 45%; connectivity 60%. Cost of capital 8.37% at the start and 8.25% in steady state. Book equity $41.3 billion, debt including leases $22.9 billion, cash $24.7 billion, 12,535 million shares. Calls the reported $28 trillion total addressable market "fantasy." An offering price near $135 a share (about $1.8 trillion) is "too richly priced" against his $1.25-$1.35 trillion range: overvalued at the rumored price. Main risk is AI overreach, magnified by Musk's more than 85% voting control.

Musk owns about 42% of equity and about 80% of the votes. At $1.25 trillion EV: about 80x sales and 156x EBITDA. Segment assumptions: launch market $30 billion growing to $100 billion by 2036, share falling from over 80% to 70%, margin 40%; Starlink internet market $15 billion to $160 billion, share 75%, margin near 60% (about 10,000 satellites and over 10 million subscribers at end-2025); xAI 2036 revenue $80 billion at a 50% margin; expansion options $50 billion of revenue at a 30% margin after 2032. notes.title: Update on NRP, Variable Dividends, Buybacks and Soda Ash
notes.text: Reported Q2 earnings Aug 5, 2026; cash distributions set to rise. Debt and preferred stock have nearly been paid off after a turnaround that began in 2015. Owns about 13 million acres of mineral rights, a cost-free royalty on future output. He calls it a "remarkable turnaround" poised to become a "capital return engine" and says earning power was hidden because most cash went to debt repayment. Credits Nat Stewart's research for making the thesis "hit me over the head obvious." Free cash flow per share and valuation are paywalled.

notes.title: AI Fear Trade, Emotional Markets, Avoiding Value Traps, and Current Opportunities
notes.text: Holds it and calls it a great business. Expects debt to be eliminated soon and much larger distributions in 2026, with variable distributions of roughly 100% of free cash flow over time. Trailing free cash flow about $16 per unit (decade average about $18) despite weak coal and soda ash markets. At $124 per unit that is about a 13% yield on trailing free cash flow. Royalty FCF margins above 90%; most cash flow is met coal, with some thermal coal.

notes.title: Thoughts on Market Valuations, AI, Productivity and Shortages
notes.text: Look reasonably valued on P/E but quite expensive on price to free cash flow. Companies now need about 5x the capital to grow a dollar of sales versus a decade ago, so ROIC is falling as capex rises. Low confidence in the returns on the capex; expects cuts eventually. He plans to stay on the sidelines.

notes.title: Contrarian Low-Cost Producer at a 15% FCF Yield + Excess Real Estate
notes.text: His main pick. Low-cost producer with about 60% share in its region and natural barriers to competition. 15% FCF yield (6.8x FCF), healthy balance sheet, uses free cash flow for buybacks, and benefits from new legislation effective Jan 1, 2026. After the Berry deal, about $80 a share of proven reserves (PV-10) against a $43 stock price. Also has excess real estate and a "call option" on extra revenue streams. Long-life, low-decline production versus shale.

notes.title: Weekend Thoughts: Malone's Born to Be Wired Book; Thoughts on Cable; Is CHTR Cheap?
notes.text: Has never owned it. About $126 a share, roughly 4x free cash flow (about $31 per share last year). Management plans to cut capex from about $11.5B to $8B, which he doubts is sustainable. Buying Cox; his napkin math puts combined FCF near $64 a share, about 50% of market cap. About $100B of debt, so it trades like a call option on revenue stability. Down 42% in ten years. He stays on the sidelines. Starlink and Amazon Leo (up to 1 Gbps) are potential threats to cable broadband.
